fact: Primary method to meet minimum spend is using card for everyday purchases (groceries, gas, dining, travel, home improvements) and bulk household items

fact: Timing charitable donations during minimum spend window enables progress toward bonus while receiving tax deduction

fact: Single hard inquiry: 3-10 points off FICO (varies by profile). Inquiry effect lasts 12 months, then fades; stops affecting score after 24 months. Multiple inquiries: 3-8 points each, compound: 6 inquiries in 12 months = 25-45 point total loss
value: 1 inquiry: 3-10 pts (12 month effect); 6 in 12 months: 25-45 pts

fact: New account penalties: hard inquiry ~5 pts, new credit penalty 10-20 pts (15 avg for Fico 8), plus AAoA reduction. Net effect neutral within 3-6 months as account ages and reports clean payments
value: Initial penalty: 15-25 pts total; recovery 3-6 months

topic: Credit Score - Average Age of Accounts Impact
fact: AAoA is 15% of FICO, 9% of VantageScore. New account drops AAoA: thin file can see 1-3 point penalty, thick file 1-3 point penalty. Effect stabilizes within 3-6 months
value: AAoA penalty: 1-3 pts; recovers in 3-6 months

fact: Utilization = 30% of FICO score (second most important after payment history). Reducing from 50% to 10% adds 20-50 points often within one billing cycle. Ideal: under 10%, excellent scores (800+) average under 3%. Monthly resets, fastest-moving factor
value: 30% of score; 20-50 pts for 50%→10% reduction; resets monthly

topic: Credit Score - Closing vs Downgrading Card
fact: Closing card lowers score by reducing available credit (utilization increase) and shortening AAoA. Downgrading (product change) preserves account history, age, and limit with zero impact; preferred strategy to avoid annual fees
value: Closing: negative impact; Downgrading: zero impact

fact: Sign-up bonuses that require minimum spending are typically treated as rebates and not taxable income (offset purchase costs)
value: Spend-required bonuses: typically NOT taxable

fact: Sign-up bonuses without spending requirement (e.g., $200 for account opening) are treated as miscellaneous income and taxable
value: No-spend bonuses: TAXABLE as ordinary income

fact: Form 1099-MISC must be issued if taxable rewards total $600+ (2025 threshold), rising to $2,000 for 2026 tax year. However, all qualifying taxable income must be reported even without 1099 form
value: 2026 threshold: $2,000; reporting required regardless

fact: Business card bonuses with spending requirement treated as rebates, not taxable. Card issuers report non-purchase rewards $600+ (rising to $2,000 in 2026) on 1099-MISC. No 1099s issued for purchase-based cash back/points/miles as they're rebates
value: Spend-based: not taxable; no-spend: reportable at $2k+ threshold

fact: Average credit card APR in 2026: 19.35-24.94% depending on data source. Q2 2026: 20.94%. Excellent credit (740+): 17-21%. Good credit (670-739): 21-24%. Rates down from 2024 record of 21.76%
value: Average: 19-25% APR; Excellent: 17-21%; Good: 21-24%

fact: If carrying balance at average 20% APR, interest cost quickly exceeds rewards value. Example: $5,000 balance at 20% = $1,000/year interest; need 2% cash back on $50,000 spend to break even on interest alone
value: 20% APR interest cost exceeds 1-2% rewards for most spenders

fact: Retention offers typically include statement credits, bonus points, or fee waivers. Success requires calling retention department and expressing dissatisfaction or intent to cancel. Spending a few minutes on phone with issuer is high ROI
value: Common: $50-300 statement credits or equivalent points

fact: Most issuers offer product change to lower-tier or no-fee version in same family; preserves account history, credit limit, age; typically ineligible for welcome offer on downgraded card. Amex: 30-day refund window; Barclays: 60-day window
value: 30-60 day refund window; zero credit score impact
